feedback: This grade cannot be completed because the submitted link only contains one of the four required deliverables. The capstone URL resolves to a single file, D4-Ethics-Stance.pdf, a single page carrying the header 'Stage 2 D4 Adegbite Adeyemi Sodiq UBI-2026-0514'. There is no D1 Findings catalogue, no D2 exploit chain with CVSS vectors, and no D3 report at this link, and no folder view that would expose the other files, so I have no readable text for three of the four deliverables and per the read reliability rule a partial read is cannotAssess, not a low score. On the one deliverable I could read, D4, the work is genuinely strong and worth saying so. The intern answers all four ethics prompts in their own voice, declines the journalist with a clear rationale that off the record is not a protected channel in a live incident, scopes what goes in writing to findings tied to line numbers and timestamps for Bayo Ogunyemi and Amaka Eze, handles the colleague timeline evidence by presenting it factually rather than weaponising it, and commits to naming the breach duty regardless of internal preference. They cite ISC2 Canon I and Canon II by their substance and anchor the essay to their own findings, the 312 customers and a decoded exfil figure of about 63 million naira. Two things to tighten in D4 even though I cannot score it: cite the ISC2 canons by NUMBER load bearing as the key requires, which they do partly, and name the NDPA 2023 duty by SECTION, specifically section 40 to notify the regulator within 72 hours and section 41 to notify affected data subjects on high risk, rather than the looser 'statutory window' and 'NITDA' phrasing, since the supervisory authority under the NDPA 2023 is the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, the NDPC, not NITDA. The single most important fix is to resubmit a link that contains all four deliverables, D1 through D4, so the capstone can actually be graded, because right now only D4 is reachable and a Stage 2 capstone cannot be marked on the ethics essay alone.
